single_hypothesis: Small-shape points (1/5 gap ~2.3us vs field) are partly per-core start/finish synchronization spread: using fewer AIV cores when per-task traffic is tiny cuts kernel wall time.
horizontal_evidence: Leaderboard ranks 1-15 all sit at 1.5-2.2us on points 1/5; only the bottom 2-3 teams (incl. us) at 3.6-4.2. This is a conventional-technique gap, not heroics. Reference TileLang impl uses coarse grids (blk_n=32 x blk_h=128 -> few blocks) while our host spreads small shapes across up to 32-48 cores.
changed_mechanism: host-only: when bytes-per-task (tileLength*rowBlock*(m+1)*2) < 8KB, blockDim = min(previous, ceil(totalBytes/8KB), >=1); kernel binary untouched (identical objects to E5)

build.kernel_objects: identical to E5 (4 kernels, host-only change)

validation.correctness: loop partition task = blockIdx + k*blockDim is a disjoint exact cover for any blockDim>=1; simulator bins unchanged (tiling-time change only)

readback_rules: Point 1 drops >=0.5us -> hypothesis confirmed, tune quantum (16KB variant next). Point 1 unchanged -> core spread is not the cost; revert to E5 host and proceed to D2. Point 1 worse by >0.3us -> refuted strongly, revert.
